participants.VISITOR: a woman on the platform, seen once as a soft shape through the ticket-window glass (Bubley 1943 figure)

fixture.outcome: goal not achieved; key remains on hook; SERVICE door stays closed

events.fact: The clerk, at his desk, has the memo '4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.' before him.
events.cue: P1: handmade memo slip on the ledger, legible pencil lines; clerk seated, pencil at temple, eyes down.
events.interpretation: He has a job to do at 4:15: fetch the key from the cupboard and open the service door.

events.fact: The clerk gets up and leaves the desk, heading across the office toward the cupboard and the SERVICE door.
events.cue: P2: same view as P1, the desk left empty but for the memo, only his shoulder leaving the right edge; P3: he walks, standing (cut at the waist by the panel edge), past the closed double cupboard whose right leaf carries the SERVICE card; no desk in frame.
events.interpretation: He is going for the key.

events.fact: A visitor outside the ticket window asks 'What time is it?'. (Film only: the counter bell rings once before.)
events.cue: P4: nobody is drawn behind the TICKET OFFICE glass; the balloon tail runs out of the panel's left edge through the window to the platform; the clerk's head, tipped up toward the voice, enters at the right edge.
events.interpretation: Someone on the platform has stopped him on his way.

events.fact: The clerk answers 'Ten past four!'; the office clock reads 4:10.
events.cue: P5: clock on the wall at 4:10 (its own hands re-set on the arbor); balloon tail to the clerk's mouth.
events.interpretation: It is five minutes before the 4:15 job.

events.fact: 'Thanks!' comes from outside; the visitor is gone.
events.cue: P6: the ticket window now empty (no figure behind the glass); balloon tail exits the panel's left edge.
events.interpretation: She has left; the interruption is over.

events.fact: The clerk reaches the cupboard; its door is open on its jamb and the brass key hangs on its hook inside the door, tagged SERVICE.
events.cue: P7: door swung open on the left jamb; key and SERVICE tag on the hook on the door's inner face; clerk arriving at right; SERVICE card on the closed door beside it.

events.outcome: goal lost: key stays on its hook, SERVICE door stays closed
events.fact: Before the open cupboard, pencil to chin, the clerk asks himself 'Now... what did I come over here for?'. The key stays on its hook; the service door stays closed.
events.cue: P8: key on its hook on the open door at left, unmoved from P7; his eyes cast down at the shelves, away from it; pencil at his chin; SERVICE card on the still-closed door; balloon tail to his mouth.
events.interpretation: The interruption made him forget the key.

seed: section-10 station incident as re-told by Direction 2: visitor, brass key, service door stays closed kept; bell is a sound cue only; envelope and bench dropped; key stays on its hook in the cupboard.
staging_notes: r1 (editor): P5 and P8 show the clerk un-mirrored (facing right): in P5 he faces the clock, in P8 he faces away from the key on the door at his left; P4 and P3 show head and torso only (the pencil hand below the frame).

SERVICE door = the right-hand leaf of the Rothstein double cupboard, carrying the handmade SERVICE sign-card; the key cupboard is its left leaf. (plan.md section 5 placed the SERVICE door at P8's far left edge; it sits at P8's upper right instead, still visible and closed.)

P8 head keeps its photographed angle (eyes cast down to the shelves); no 2D roll of the head, per the test-shot note. No second photograph of this agent exists at LoC (searched); no replacement head was found that matches.
